correctness.rationale: For each triple the unique fourth completion exists. A nonblock four-set has four distinct external completion points because two coinciding completions would form blocks with three common points. Moving one of four pebbles leaves at most three fixed points, so every equality/completion/generic category occurs in all SQS orders >=8. Moving one of five pebbles leaves at most four fixed points; a fixed block allows only generic fresh points; a nonblock fixed four allows its four completions and v-8 generic points, with all five fresh types present precisely when v>=10 and the generic type absent in both order-eight systems. The explicit five-variable formula requiring a generic fifth point over a nonblock four-set holds iff v>=10. A permanent two-sided pebble strategy and the standard pebble/FO correspondence cover all quantifier depths. Local extension catalogues were fully enumerated for SQS8, SQS10, SQS16 and showed exactly these differences. Those finite checks are corroboration, not a proof for all systems.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of all finite nontrivial Steiner quadruple systems in a standard model-theoretic invariant. It identifies one unconditional FO^4 class, exactly two FO^5 classes, and the sharp 8-to-10 transition via the combinatorics of four distinct triple completions. No classification of individual block arrangements is needed, despite an unbounded family with many nonisomorphic members. The exact variable-width inexpressibility is motivated by the relational arity and uniqueness axiom, rather than a narrow arbitrary count or a software benchmark.
